title: Aurora Health - Postmortem follow-up (Oct 11 2027)
summary: Follow-up on the Sept 29 outage impacting inference latency for Aurora Health. Reviewed root cause timeline, short-term mitigation (routing fallback + rate limiting), and long-term reliability improvements (KV cache monitoring, autoscale policy tweaks, canary rollout for quantized variant). Agreed owners and dates for benchmarks, security artifact exchange, and a pilot for Dedicated capacity on a small pool.
topics: Rollout plan for fixes and canary
next_steps: Maya to send postmortem doc and timeline link (drive) by 2027-10-13
Ravi to run replay benchmarks and share latency/cost histograms by 2027-10-18
Aurora to provide firewall and LB logs for the spike (Ethan) by 2027-10-13
Claire to schedule weekly check-ins for next 4 weeks and invite stakeholders by 2027-10-12
Security teams (Samir + Redwood security) to exchange SOC2 summary and KMS diagram by 2027-10-15
action_items: Maya Chen - Send consolidated postmortem doc + links - due 2027-10-13
Ravi Patel - Replay afternoon spike against staging and produce histogram + KV hit-rate by 2027-10-18
Ethan Park (Aurora) - Share firewall and load balancer logs for spike window (09/29 02:14-02:22 UTC) - due 2027-10-13
Samir Khan (Aurora) - Confirm encryption at rest key management and provide KMS contact - due 2027-10-15
Claire Gomez - Create weekly check-in invite and attach postmortem summary - due 2027-10-12
header: Date: 2027-10-11T15:00Z | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood), Ravi Patel (Redwood), Claire Gomez (Redwood CSM), Janelle Ortiz (Aurora), Ethan Park (Aurora SRE), Samir Khan (Aurora Security), Lina Torres (Aurora)
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll go quick, this is the aurora postmortem follow-up. we have ravi and claire from our side, and i see janelle, ethan, samir, lina, thanks for making time
[00:18] Janelle Ortiz: yeah thanks maya, want to make sure we cover the timeline and what you guys changed last week, and next steps for stability

[00:28] Ravi Patel: cool, i'll kick off with the timeline i have, apologies if some names are off in the auto transcript, but on 2027-09-29 at ~02:14 UTC we saw a sudden latency spike, p95 went from 180ms to about 2.1s across a subset of routes
[00:50] Ravi Patel: initial look showed a thundering herd hitting a cold KV cache after a deploy, also some concurrent retries from the client side which amplified load

[01:07] Ethan Park: just to clarify, those retries were from our side — a retry policy that ramps quickly under timeout. we have the config and can adjust but wanted to understand the root cause first

[01:25] Maya Chen: noted, ethan. short-term we pushed a routing fallback to a lower-latency quantized variant and enabled a restrictive rate limit for that route, which brought p95 back under SLO in about 12 minutes, correct ravi?

[01:46] Ravi Patel: yes, fallback + small bump to autoscale and the rate limit cut the noise. also we warmed the KV cache by replaying recent prefixes. the replay process had some transcription issues in logs (KV cash was logged in one place), so we cleaned that up
[02:10] Lina Torres: when you say quantized variant, is that the 4-bit we tested? we saw some quality diffs in staging but not huge

[02:22] Ravi Patel: it's the 4-bit INT4 variant with the new kernel selection. for this route we had a pinned full-precision model that didn't scale as well, so the fallback used quantized variant on Dedicated, sorry deicated pool in one region — auto transcript says Deicated earlier
[02:44] Samir Khan: security question: did the fallback change any data residency or encryption behavior? we need to sign off that no keys left aurora's KMS boundary
[02:58] Maya Chen: good call. short answer: no, we used the same VPC and the same KMS (customer-managed) — no change. we'll send the KMS diagram for the flow. samir — we'll add that to action items
[03:15] Janelle Ortiz: can you walk through the RCA briefly? the timeline is good but we need to tie causal chain to the mitigation so we can update our internal docs

[03:29] Ravi Patel: RCA summary: 1) a deploy changed a caching key prefix in a small microservice, 2) traffic shifted and expired many KV entries, 3) client-side retry policy amplified, 4) autoscaler reaction lagged because the request pattern was bursty leading to queueing, and 5) monitoring alerting thresholds didn't catch the degraded tail early enough
[03:59] Maya Chen: and we field-fixed with routing fallback, rate limit, and manual cache warm, and then adjusted autoscale throttle to be more aggressive for short bursts

[04:12] Ethan Park: we appreciate that, but for long term we need changes on both sides. we'll reduce our retry multiplier and maybe add jitter. also want to understand the cost implications if we move more weight to Dedicated pools

[04:29] Ravi Patel: absolutely — moving to Dedicated or reserved capacity reduces noisy neighbor risk and gives predictable throughput; cost model is commit-based. we gave rough numbers in the doc, but we'll send a detailed cost/perf spreadsheet
[04:47] Janelle Ortiz: were any requests lost or is it pure latency? compliance needs to know if any PII was exposed or dropped

[04:58] Claire Gomez: we confirmed no data exfiltration and no request bodies were stored outside aurora retention policies. standard audit logs captured the event — we'll share the log slices with samir
[05:15] Samir Khan: i'll need the SOC 2 summary and the audit log retention policy. plus a KMS contact for key rotation questions
[05:28] Maya Chen: noted — action: send SOC2 summary + KMS diagram (maya) by 10/13

[05:35] Ravi Patel: next, benchmarks — we'll replay the spike against a staging environment instrumented with the same autoscale windows; expected outputs: latency histogram, queue length over time, KV hit rate, GPU utilization
[05:54] Lina Torres: what does the replay use as traffic fidelity? we need to be sure it's realistic — headers, auth tokens, and payload shapes
[06:05] Ravi Patel: good point. we'll replay synthetically but will ask aurora to share a sanitized slice of the real traffic so we preserve shapes; ethan — can you help provide a sanitized sample?
[06:17] Ethan Park: yes, we can do a scrubbed sample. i'll add that to the logs package request
[06:25] Janelle Ortiz: i'd also like to see a canary plan for rolling the kernel selection fix. we don't want a big blast radius if the fix has perf regressions

[06:36] Ravi Patel: proposed canary: 1% traffic for 48 hours to quantized variant with strict monitoring hooks, then 10% for 24 hours, then 50% if stable. auto rollback if p95 crosses threshold or token cost delta > 8%
[06:57] Maya Chen: and we can instrument with the console traces and our rollout API to do an automatic fallback on anomalies — we showed that in the demo deck last quarter
[07:10] Ethan Park: cost questions: nina from finance will ask about egress and token unit changes when we move to Dedicated plus quantization. who owns that estimate?
[07:22] Maya Chen: i'll own a first-pass estimate and ravi will provide per-token latency/cost from the benchmark; we'll put a spreadsheet in the drive
[07:34] Janelle Ortiz: security again — samir needs the list of infra components touched during mitigation. was any new role or RBAC policy created?

[07:44] Ravi Patel: no new RBAC created. we used existing service roles. mitigation touched routing config, autoscale settings, and a temporary rate limit rule. we'll document each change in the postmortem doc
[08:00] Samir Khan: ok please add the ACL and RBAC snapshot to the artifacts
[08:08] Claire Gomez: i'll collect and attach artifacts in one place — postmortem doc + logs + replay results + SOC2 summary

[08:19] Maya Chen: timeline for fixes — short term: config changes and replay by 10/18; medium term: implement autoscale policy improvements and a KV cache warm strategy by 10/25; long term: plan pilot on a small Dedicated pool and evaluate cost/throughput by 11/08
[08:40] Lina Torres: about the KV warm strategy, can we have a progressive warm where we prime hot prefixes first? full warm can be expensive
[08:51] Ravi Patel: yes, progressive warm by prefix frequency is what we've been prototyping. the runtime supports prefix-aware warming and we'll add a metric for cold-miss spikes
[09:05] Ethan Park: i want to confirm alerts — during the incident our paging threshold didn't fire quickly; what metrics will change?
[09:15] Ravi Patel: we'll add a tail-latency alert (p95 and p99 delta over baseline) and add KV miss-rate threshold; also monitor queue lengths to detect queueing before GPU saturation
[09:30] Janelle Ortiz: good. about Dedicated pilot: how disruptive is it to route a percentage of production traffic?
[09:40] Maya Chen: not disruptive — we can route specific routes or experiment IDs to the Dedicated pool. traffic split is handled at the request router and can be reversed instantly if needed
[09:53] Samir Khan: audit question: who will have access to logs in Dedicated? RBAC should map to our SSO groups — SAML config or SAMl (auto mis-transcript) needs to be confirmed
[10:04] Claire Gomez: we'll include the SSO/SAML mapping doc in the artifacts. samir, we'll need your IAM contact to finalize mapping
[10:13] Ethan Park: one more operational ask: after the replay, can you produce a short runbook for our oncall to follow if latency rises?
[10:22] Ravi Patel: yes, we'll produce a 1-page runbook: key metrics to check, quick mitigation steps (enable fallback, tighten rate limit, scale pool), and contact list
[10:33] Maya Chen: ok let's recap the explicit next steps and owners — and then open the floor for questions
[10:40] Janelle Ortiz: quick question — any change to data retention or request logging we should expect?
[10:48] Claire Gomez: no changes to retention. logs we share will be scrubbed and matched to aurora retention policies
[10:56] Lina Torres: will you prioritize the autoscale policy change over the Dedicated pilot?
[11:03] Maya Chen: yes, autoscale tweaks are medium-term and quicker to deploy; pilot requires procurement however we can start a low-cost pilot in parallel
[11:14] Samir Khan: for procurement, is there a legal/contract addendum for Dedicated?
[11:20] Maya Chen: there is a simple addendum for reserved capacity and SLA terms, we can share a template — action for maya to send it

[11:28] Ravi Patel: technical note: we discovered one of our kernels had a subtle memory spike when certain sequence lengths hit 1k tokens; doesn't explain full event but worth guarding against. we'll bump a guard in the runtime to prevent that kernel for long sequences until patched
[11:48] Lina Torres: that's the kind of detail we want in the RCA, thanks
[11:55] Janelle Ortiz: anything else? if not i'll hand to samir for security closeout
[12:01] Samir Khan: nothing else from me, just two asks: SOC2 artifact and KMS contact. once we have those i'll sign off on the mitigation plan and the pilot
[12:12] Maya Chen: great — we'll send both by 10/15. last thing — we'll schedule weekly 30-minute check-ins for 4 weeks starting 10/12 to track progress
[12:25] Claire Gomez: calendar invites out by tomorrow
[12:30] Janelle Ortiz: thanks all, appreciate the quick response from redwood team
[12:36] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned
